mainTopic: Whether רב יהודה's lenient ruling on a מבוי that ends in a רחבה can follow רב, given רב's own stricter ruling on a מבוי breached into a חצר
overview: On the previous amud, אביי asked רב יוסף whose view רב יהודה followed when he ruled that a מבוי ending in a רחבה needs nothing more to permit carrying. The גמרא explains that if the ruling is רב's, then רב seems to contradict himself. רב ruled that a מבוי breached along its whole width into a חצר, with the חצר breached opposite it, is אסור. Why not treat that מבוי like one ending in a רחבה? רב יוסף answers that he does not know the source. He only knows of a real case in a shepherds' village where רב יהודה required nothing. So the ruling can simply be credited to שמואל, and there is no difficulty. The גמרא then uses רב ששת's distinction between a case with an עירוב and a case without one. With it, the גמרא shows that רב does not contradict himself: when the חצר and מבוי residents made a joint עירוב the מבוי is permitted, and when they did not it is forbidden.

steps.title: If the ruling is רב's, he contradicts himself twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא warns that tying רב יהודה's lenient ruling to רב creates a double contradiction with רב's other statements.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it is a ruling of רב, then רב contradicts רב in two ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it matters whose view רב יהודה followed. It is setting up the contradiction it will spell out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה ruled that a מבוי ending in a רחבה needs nothing more to permit carrying. If that ruling is רב's, it clashes with two other statements of רב. Only one of those two clashes is quoted in the text that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: one statement of רב against another statement of רב

steps.confusionAlert: The text says 'two' contradictions but quotes only one, the breach case. According to the commentators, the other contradiction is that a רחבה opens to the public domain, which makes the מבוי open at both ends (מבוי מפולש). רב requires a stronger fix for that kind of מבוי.

phrases.english: For if it is a ruling of Rav,
there is a contradiction of Rav against Rav in two ways:

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי דְּרַב קַשְׁיָא דְּרַב אַדְּרַב בְּתַרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains אביי's earlier question about whose view רב יהודה followed (on the previous amud).
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing רב יהודה's ruling on a מבוי ending in a רחבה to רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's other rulings are stricter, so this lenient ruling cannot easily be his.

steps.title: רב's ruling on a מבוי breached into a חצר
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a מבוי's back wall is fully breached into a חצר, and the חצר is breached opposite it, carrying is allowed in the חצר but not in the מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: if a מבוי was breached along its full width into a חצר, and the חצר was breached opposite it, the חצר is permitted and the מבוי is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the statement of רב that it will use to build the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מבוי has lost its back wall, so it now opens into a חצר, and that חצר opens out on the far side. The חצר stays permitted, but רב forbids carrying in the מבוי. This strict ruling is what clashes with רב יהודה's lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: an alleyway that courtyards open into

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
An alleyway that was breached along its full width into a courtyard,
and the courtyard was breached opposite it,
the courtyard is permitted and the alleyway is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the contradiction announced in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי fully breached into a חצר that is breached opposite it is forbidden, while the חצר stays permitted.

steps.title: Why not treat it like a מבוי ending in a רחבה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב forbids the breached מבוי when, by רב יהודה's ruling, a מבוי ending in a רחבה is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let it be like a מבוי that ends in a רחבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes the contradiction explicit. The breached מבוי looks just like a מבוי that ends in an open backyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the far end of the מבוי opens into an enclosed area that leads outward. If רב permits one, he should permit the other. Forbidding the breached מבוי while permitting the רחבה case looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: that ends in a backyard or enclosed open area

phrases.english: And why?
Let it be like an alleyway that ends in a backyard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling from step 2 to complete the attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the breached מבוי is אסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The breached case is the same as the רחבה case, so the rulings should match.

steps.title: רב יוסף only knows the story, not the source
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he does not know whose view it was. He only knows of a case in a shepherds' village where רב יהודה required nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I do not know. There was an incident in a shepherds' village with a מבוי that ended in a רחבה. It came before רב יהודה, and he did not require anything at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי that he only knows about the practical ruling, not whose view it followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף confirms that the ruling is real: רב יהודה really did permit the מבוי without any fix. He does not know whether רב יהודה learned it from רב or from שמואל. That opens the door for the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not require anything at all

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know;
there was an incident in a shepherds' village
where there was an alleyway ending in a backyard,
and it came before Rav Yehuda,
and he did not require anything at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question behind steps 1 through 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב יהודה followed רב or שמואל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף does not know; he only knows of the actual ruling.

steps.title: Attribute the ruling to שמואל instead
steps.stepSummary: If tying the ruling to רב is difficult, say that רב יהודה ruled in the name of שמואל, and the difficulty disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is difficult in the name of רב, let it be in the name of שמואל, and there is no difficulty at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a simple way out: רב יהודה had two teachers, so credit the ruling to the other one, שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only exists if the ruling is רב's. Since רב יהודה was a student of both רב and שמואל, the ruling can follow שמואל, who has no conflicting statement. The contradiction is avoided without explaining רב at all.

phrases.english: And if it is difficult in the name of Rav,
let it be in the name of Shmuel,
and there is no difficulty at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי קַשְׁיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב תֶּיהְוֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יוסף's uncertainty from step 4 to offer a resolution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution of the ruling to a different authority
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling is רב's, so רב contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling may follow שמואל, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב ששת's distinction: with an עירוב or without one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls רב ששת's explanation of רב's statement: one case is where they made an עירוב, the other where they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that רב ששת said to רב שמואל בר אבא (and some say to רב יוסף בר אבא): I will explain it to you. Here it is where they made an עירוב; there it is where they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in רב ששת's earlier distinction. It is setting up a new answer that will defend רב directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת had explained רב's breach ruling by splitting it into two cases. In one case the residents made an עירוב, and in the other they did not. The word הַשְׁתָּא ('now that') signals that this tool will now solve our contradiction too.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (it was said) to
I will explain it to you
they made an עירוב joining their domains

phrases.english: Now that Rav Sheshet said
to Rav Shmuel bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: and some say to Rav Yosef bar Abba:
I will explain it to you:
here, where they made an eiruv;
there, where they did not make an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second approach that defends רב instead of switching to שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rulings about a breached מבוי depend on whether an עירוב was made.

steps.title: No contradiction in רב: it depends on a joint עירוב
steps.stepSummary: Using רב ששת's distinction, the גמרא resolves the contradiction. Where the חצר and מבוי residents made a joint עירוב, the מבוי is permitted. Where they did not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב against רב is also not difficult. Here, the residents of the חצר made an עירוב with the residents of the מבוי; there, they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב יהודה's ruling can follow רב after all, because the two rulings deal with different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a joint עירוב, the חצר and the מבוי act as one shared domain, so a מבוי opening into it is fine. That is רב יהודה's lenient case. Without a joint עירוב, the חצר residents become new, unjoined residents of the מבוי and forbid carrying there. That is רב's strict breach ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gives two ways to avoid a contradiction: credit רב יהודה's ruling to שמואל, or keep it with רב and explain the difference by the עירוב. With a joint עירוב the מבוי is permitted; without one it is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether carrying is allowed can depend on the people (whether residents joined in an עירוב), not only on the walls and openings.

phrases.english: Rav against Rav is also not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — שֶׁעֵירְבוּ בְּנֵי חָצֵר עִם בְּנֵי מָבוֹי,
phrases.english: here, where the courtyard residents made an eiruv with the alleyway residents;
there, where they did not make an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב ששת's distinction from step 6 to the contradiction raised in steps 1 through 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by עירוב status)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's strict breach ruling and רב יהודה's lenient ruling describe the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ruling applies when a joint עירוב was made; the strict one applies when it was not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה's ruling can follow רב, since רב does not contradict himself once the עירוב status is taken into account.
